svg.title: Content installation — mechanism and order
svg.desc: How the four content types install: which mechanism each uses, why they are serialised, where the server is stopped, and what is still unsolved. Companion to operation-model-roadmap.svg, which tracks ticket state rather than behaviour. Update when the behaviour changes, not when a ticket moves.
svg.text: Content installation — mechanism and order
Four content types, two mechanisms. What runs when, what waits for what, and why.
Companion to operation-model-roadmap.svg: that one tracks tickets, this one tracks behaviour. Cite a file:line before changing a box.
1 · System install
The rootfs is laid down.
Nothing else can be running:
there is no box yet. Orders
chosen before this are banked.
2 · proot — Ansible
Maps and app modules.
A runrole owns the rootfs.
Always first: everything REST
waits until this is idle.
3 · Server up
Started, or already up.
The REST core answers
at /k2go-api/.
4 · REST — in-server
ZIM · Books · Courses.
One at a time: each defers while
another holds a session, so three
size checks cannot all pass at once.
WHY REST WAITS
Ansible forks background processes, so concurrent REST work
risks corruption — not because the server is down.
ADFA-4900 · ZimProvisioner.drain():42
DELIBERATE DEVIATION
A maps-only batch does NOT stop the server
Maps adds tiles and never touches the REST core, so it is
carved out to avoid a pointless bounce. Any other module
(courses app, calibre-web) still does stop → runroles → restart.
InstallService.runModuleQueue():704
OPEN
No run-level disk budget
Each selector does block: it compares its own total against StatFs at the moment it is opened. But a banked order is not on disk yet, so two
selections can each fit and jointly overflow — and the one that drains second dies mid-download with tens of GB already written.
The wizard DOES show the running total ("Your picks 9.4 GB"); what none of them does is subtract it before deciding. The sum informs, it does not guard.
And serialising is not the safety net it looks like: ZimProvisioner.drain starts asynchronously (catalogue fetch first), so in the
same orchestrateStep pass Books and Courses see no session yet and start too. Observed on device: three streams at once.
ZimConfirmFragment:94 · MapsChooseFragment:270 · KolibriConfirmFragment:211 — three readings, three moments, no total
Noted, not blocking: nice-to-have, and the real answer is the budget rather than tighter serialising. Do not let it displace the ticket.
OPEN
One host after confirming — ADFA-5074, the landings are done
Wizard, all four types: the order is banked and the user returns to the hub. No progress surface at all until after the install.
Get More, all four types: the door starts the work and hands off to SetupProgressActivity. Maps and the modules always did; Books
since ADFA-4988; Courses and ZIM moved here. What differed was the host, so Back walked out of a live download and a notification
returned you to a screen you had not left. The screens themselves never were duplicated — openDetail() hosted the same fragments.
The index is now the router: every door and every notification lands here, so openDetail() is reachable only by tapping a row. The
row carries the transfer rate — the one thing that separates "slow" from "stopped" for someone who left and came back in an hour.
A busy door now BANKS instead of refusing. The wishlist is the queue — each provisioner defers while another stream holds the line,
and two pumps drain it: the index, and the Home (which had never included courses, so a banked courses order could sit forever).
ADFA-5074 is closed. Follow-ups: the Books "downloads" viewer (needs an idle index) · a busy Kolibri reads as absent · no rate for Books.
FIXED — WAS SUBTLE
A finished run could not close itself
Completion is a fact about the run. It was gated on three things that are about something else, and each alone stalled the redirect:
servicesReady — a gate on STARTING work, gating the admission that work had ENDED. Its probe gives the box 2.5 s while the box is
busy serving the very download in question, so a slow link read as "Starting services." over a green Done row. REST starts nothing.
The poll was posted only when the index was on top — but the hint route opened a detail during onCreate. And render() returned early
under a detail, so a run finishing there had nowhere to say so. nothingToStart() · onResume posts unconditionally · render steps back.
Which type is which
Maps — proot
runrole, tiles
ZIM / Wikipedia — REST
Books — REST
Courses (Kolibri) — REST
The courses APP is a proot module;
its CONTENT is REST. One name,
two mechanisms — the distinction
the operation model exists for.
Caveat on the names
The model calls the two classes
LIVE and STOPPED, which names
them after the consequence.
Maps breaks that: it runs under
proot and the server stays up.
The real axis is the mechanism
(proot vs REST); stopping the box
is a consequence that depends on
which module is in the batch.
Reading it the other way is what
this map exists to prevent.
